description: From zero code to a deployed responsive website.

weeks.weekTheme: The Anatomy of a Web Page (HTML5)

lessons.title: The Web & The Skeleton
lessons.topic: How the internet works & the HTML boilerplate.
teaches: The Client-Server relationship (Request vs. Response).
Setting up VS Code and installing the 'Live Server' extension.
The standard boilerplate: <!DOCTYPE html>, <html>, <head>, and <body>.
The concept of 'Tags': Opening <tag>, Content, and Closing </tag>.
checklist: Can explain that the user only sees what is inside the <body> tag.
Can create an 'index.html' file from scratch.
Can type '!' + Tab in VS Code to generate boilerplate instantly.
Can launch Live Server and see their text in Chrome.
lessons.teacherPrep: Bring a physical skeleton or a cardboard box. Explain: 'HTML is the skeleton; it has no skin, no makeup, and cannot move. It just holds the shape.'

lessons.title: Text & Semantic Hierarchy
teaches: Headings: <h1> through <h6> (The rule of only one H1 per page).

Paragraphs (

), Line breaks (
), and Horizontal rules (

).
Visual vs. Semantic bold/italics (<b> vs <strong>, <i> vs <em>).
How to write comments and why we leave notes for our future selves.
checklist: Understands that H1-H6 dictates importance, not just visual size.

Can properly nest tags without crossing them (e.g.,

...

).
Can write a 3-paragraph 'News Article' using correct heading tiers.
lessons.teacherPrep:
Give them a printed, unformatted Wikipedia article. Have them take a red pen and mark what should be an H1, an H2, and a

.

lessons.title: The Anchor & The Web
teaches: The Anchor tag: <a> and the concept of 'Attributes' (href='...').
Absolute links (going to https://google.com).
Relative links (going to another file in the same folder: 'about.html').
The target='_blank' attribute to open new tabs.
Directory traversal: what './' and '../' mean.
checklist: Can link two HTML pages together back-and-forth.
Can explain why an internal link broke if a file was moved into a sub-folder.
Can create a basic 3-page site (Home, About, Contact) with a working text-menu.
lessons.teacherPrep: Create a folder on your desktop called 'House'. Inside, put 'living_room.html' and a subfolder called 'Upstairs' containing 'bedroom.html'. Have them code the walk upstairs.

lessons.title: Images & Embeds
lessons.topic: Adding rich media to the skeleton.
teaches: The self-closing tag: .
The absolute necessity of the 'alt' attribute (Screen readers & broken links).
Hotlinking (web URLs) vs. Local hosting (saving a .jpg inside an /images folder).
Embedding YouTube videos via the <iframe> tag.
checklist: Knows that self-closing tags do not get a </tag> partner.
Can render a local image stored in a sub-folder: src='./img/dog.png'.
Can inspect an image element in browser DevTools to see its natural size.
lessons.teacherPrep: Intentionally give them starter code with a typo in an image source ('catt.png'). Teach them to use Chrome DevTools Network tab to spot the 404 error.

weeks.weekTheme: HTML Data & The Intro to CSS

lessons.title: Lists & Semantic Containers
teaches: Unordered lists (<ul>), Ordered lists (<ol>), and List Items (<li>).
The concept of Parent, Child, and Sibling elements (The DOM Tree).
Moving away from 'Div soup': Semantic wrappers (<header>, <nav>, <main>, <section>, <footer>).
The generic container: <div>.
checklist: Can create a nested list (an Ordered list inside an Unordered list item).
Can look at an HTML document and draw its 'Family Tree' on a whiteboard.
Uses <nav> for links and <footer> for the bottom, rather than <div> for both.
lessons.teacherPrep: Have them write a recipe page. Ingredients must be a <ul>; the step-by-step baking instructions must be an <ol>.

lessons.title: HTML Tables
teaches: Table syntax: <table>, <thead>, <tbody>, <tr>, <th>, and <td>.
Merging cells: the 'colspan' and 'rowspan' attributes.
Historical context: Why we used tables for website layouts in 1999, and why doing it today is a sin.
checklist: Understands that <th> centers and bolds text; <td> is left-aligned standard text.
Can construct a 5-day Class Timetable, merging a 3-column block for 'Lunch Break'.
lessons.teacherPrep: Show them an old 1996 Space Jam or Yahoo screenshot. Explain how tables held the layout together before CSS existed.

lessons.title: Collecting Data (Forms Part 1)
teaches: The <form> wrapper (brief mention of 'action' and 'method').
The <input> tag and standard types: text, email, password, number.
The <label> tag and linking it to an input using 'for' and 'id'.
Checkboxes vs. Radio buttons (and grouping radios using identical 'name' attributes).
checklist: Understands that clicking a <label> should automatically focus its input box.
Can create a 'Gender selection' radio group where the user can only pick one.
Knows the difference between 'placeholder' text and a hardcoded 'value'.
lessons.teacherPrep: Open Netflix sign-up, inspect the password input field, and change type='password' to type='text' live to show them how saved passwords work.

lessons.title: Advanced Forms & Validation
lessons.topic: Dropdowns, Text areas, and keeping bad data out.
teaches: Dropdown menus: <select> and <option>.
Multi-line text: <textarea>.
Buttons: <button type='submit'> vs <button type='button'>.
Native HTML5 validation: required, minlength, maxlength, min, max.
checklist: Can build a fully functioning 'Contact Us' form.
Can make a form trigger a browser native red warning if submitted with an empty email.
lessons.teacherPrep: Assign the 'Pizza Order Form' challenge: Size (radio), toppings (checkboxes), delivery instructions (textarea), quantity (number bounded 1-10).

lessons.title: Entering CSS & Selectors
teaches: What CSS stands for and the 'Cascade' rule (bottom overrides top).
Three ways to apply CSS (Inline, Internal, External). Why External is the law.
CSS Syntax: Selector { property: value; }
The Big Three Selectors: Element (p), Class (.card), ID (#navbar).
The hierarchy of specificity: ID beats Class; Class beats Element.
checklist: Can successfully hook up a 'style.css' file to an 'index.html' file.
Can target 3 specific paragraphs out of 10 using a '.highlight' class.
Understands why an ID should only be used once per page.
lessons.teacherPrep: Explain classes vs IDs using social security numbers: 'Anyone can belong to the class .brown-hair, but only one person owns the ID #ssn-9921.'

lessons.title: Color & Typography
teaches: Color formats: Names, HEX (#ffffff), RGB, and RGBA (Alpha/transparency).
Font styling: font-family, font-size, font-weight, text-align, line-height.
Web-safe fonts vs. Importing Google Fonts via @import or <link>.
Generic fallback families (serif, sans-serif, monospace).
checklist: Can import 'Roboto' from Google Fonts into their CSS file.
Can create a translucent dark overlay box using background-color: rgba(0,0,0, 0.5).
Can remove link underlines using text-decoration: none.
lessons.teacherPrep: Give them an intentionally hideous 90s website (neon green, pink Comic Sans) and give them 20 mins to re-brand it into a luxury coffee shop.

lessons.title: The CSS Box Model
lessons.topic: The single most important concept in CSS.
teaches: The truth: Every single element on a web page is an invisible rectangle.
The Layers: Content -> Padding -> Border -> Margin.
The Box Model trap: Setting a box to 300px width + 20px padding makes it 340px wide.
The permanent global fix: * { box-sizing: border-box; }.
Using the DevTools 'Computed' tab to inspect the colored box model.
checklist: Can recite the rule: Margin is outside the border; Padding is inside the border.
Can physically draw the Box Model on a piece of scrap paper.
Can use margin: 0 auto; to horizontally center a fixed-width block.
lessons.teacherPrep: Bring a coffee mug inside a shipping box. Mug = Content. Bubble wrap touching mug = Padding. Cardboard box = Border. Empty air to the next box = Margin.

lessons.title: Display & The Normal Flow
lessons.topic: How the browser stacks boxes by default.
teaches:
Block-level elements (stack vertically, expand 100% width:
,

,

).
Inline elements (sit side-by-side, wrap tight to content: <span>, <a>, <strong>).
The hybrid: display: inline-block (sits side-by-side, but respects custom height/width).
display: none vs visibility: hidden (Deleting physical space vs leaving an invisible ghost).
checklist: Can explain why giving a standard inline <a> tag a margin-top: 50px does nothing.
Can turn an inline link into a wide, chunky clickable block button.

lessons.title: Flexbox Fundamentals
teaches: Why older layout methods (Floats) were the dark ages.
The Golden Rule: You talk to the Parent Container to move the Children.
Turning it on: display: flex.
The Main Axis vs. The Cross Axis (flex-direction: row vs column).
justify-content: flex-start, center, flex-end, space-between, space-around.
checklist: Can take a vertical <ul> of 5 links and turn it into a spaced-out horizontal Navbar in 3 lines of CSS.
Can perfectly center a small div inside a giant div both horizontally and vertically.
lessons.teacherPrep: Introduce the free browser game 'Flexbox Froggy'. Spend the last 15 minutes of class letting them clear levels 1 through 10.

lessons.title: Advanced Flexbox
teaches: Controlling the Cross-Axis: align-items (stretch, center, flex-start).
The overflow issue: flex-wrap: wrap.
The best property in modern CSS: gap: 20px (no more math with margins!).
Talking directly to the child: flex-grow and re-arranging visual flow with 'order'.
checklist: Can build a responsive '3-Card Product Showcase' that sits in one row on desktop, but snaps into 2 rows when the browser is resized.
lessons.teacherPrep: Have them finish levels 11 through 24 of Flexbox Froggy.

lessons.title: The Position Property
lessons.topic: Breaking elements out of the normal flow.
teaches: position: static (The default state of the universe).
position: relative (Moving an element relative to where it *should* have sat).
position: absolute (Searching up the DOM tree for a 'relative' parent to anchor to).
position: fixed (Locking an element to the glass of the user's monitor).
Stacking order: z-index.
checklist: Can create a 'Chat with us!' circular button locked to the bottom-right of the screen even when scrolled down.
Can put a small 'SALE' badge tucked over the top-right corner of a product card image.
lessons.teacherPrep: Use the 'Ghost escaping the body' analogy: Absolute positioning pulls the element out of the flow; its siblings slide up into its space, while its ghost floats over them.

lessons.title: Project Polish & Deployment
lessons.topic: Putting your work on the actual internet.
teaches: Final code hygiene: Indentation check, removing unused test CSS classes.
File structure standards: Root contains index.html; sub-folders for /css, /img.
Introduction to Web Hosting (Servers vs your local C:/ drive).
Free instant deployment via Netlify Drop (app.netlify.com/drop).
checklist: Can zip their project folder, drop it into Netlify, and generate a live https://xxxx.netlify.app link.
Can pull their custom website up on their own physical mobile phone to show a classmate.
lessons.teacherPrep: Remind them of Day 1: 'Today is the day you text a live URL of a website you coded by hand to your mom/partner/friend.'
